speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. How old are you, and can you point to exactly where your leg hurts? Also, did this pain start suddenly or has it been getting worse over time?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old male. Mother has noticed a change in the child’s play patterns, specifically favoring his left leg while walking or running. The child complains of pain in his left knee, but denies any recent trauma or injury. He has no fever or other systemic symptoms. Nutrition and developmental milestones are appropriate for age.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the pain seem to come from the hip or groin area instead of the knee, and is it worse when you try to turn your leg inward? Also, does he have any difficulty walking or does he prefer to keep his leg turned outward?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain localized to the left knee. I also have Limping favoring left leg, No fever, No systemic symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the pain actually feel like it's coming from your hip or groin when you try to move your leg, or is it strictly in the knee? Also, is it harder for you to turn your left leg inward, or do you naturally keep it turned outward when you walk?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical or surgical history. Social history: The patient is in the second grade, lives with parents and one younger sibling. No exposure to tobacco or known toxins.

speaker: Doctor
text: Can you tell me if you feel any pain deep in your hip or groin when I move your leg, rather than just in the knee? I also need to know if your leg feels stiff or if you naturally keep it turned outward when you walk.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies recent illness, rash, weight loss, change in appetite or urinary symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you feel any deep pain in your hip or groin when I try to rotate your leg inward, or is the pain strictly in your knee? Also, do you naturally keep your leg turned outward when you walk to avoid that pain? REQUEST TEST: Hip_X-Ray.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: The patient reports deep pain in the left hip/groin area upon internal rotation of the leg, rather than strictly knee pain, and demonstrates a tendency to externally rotate the left leg while walking to minimize discomfort. Hip X-ray findings reveal flattening and fragmentation of the left femoral head, consistent with Legg-Calvé-Perthes disease.
